issues.claim: Resource card: 'NJSBDC at Rutgers University-New Brunswick (serves Middlesex County)' and 'currently delivered virtually', cited to https://njsbdc.com/about-us/
issues.problem: The cited about-us page does not mention New Brunswick or Middlesex County (it says the State Office is hosted at Rutgers Business School in Newark and that there are seven regional centers), nor that delivery is virtual. The claims are true, but they come from a different NJSBDC page: https://njsbdc.com/njsbdc-at-rutgers-university-new-brunswick/ ('Serving Middlesex County'; 'Our Middlesex office is currently not offering in-person appointments. Our business counseling and training services remain fully operational and available virtually'). The 'nearly all of our services are provided at no cost' quote and the eRFC requirement ARE on the cited about-us page.
issues.fix: Keep the about-us URL for the free-services quote and eRFC requirement, but add (or substitute) the Rutgers-New Brunswick center URL as the source for the location/Middlesex coverage and virtual delivery.

issues.claim: Finding 5: Hinge 'Beyond Referrals' study of 1,028 buyers; over 99% check a firm out first; average more than three strategies; over 80% visit the website; 'slightly more likely' to search online than ask a friend; references least-used; social media used more than references
issues.problem: The cited hingemarketing.com blog URL returned HTTP 403 for me (twice). All the numbers are nevertheless confirmed in Hinge's own report PDF, 'Beyond Referrals: How Today's Buyers Check You Out' (Hinge Research Institute, (c)2014): 1,028 buyers, average 3.2 methods, website 80.8%, search online 63.2% vs friends/colleagues 62.4%, social media 59.9% vs seller-supplied references 55.5%, 0.7% 'I don't check them out' (i.e. ~99.3% do check). The study year is 2014, which the brief renders only as 'undated page (pre-2020 Hinge study)'.
issues.fix: Cite the report PDF (https://rlhb.lexblogplatformthree.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/111/2014/02/HIN-BeyondReferrals-Report-021314-1.pdf) alongside the blog URL, and label the finding 2014 (not just 'pre-2020') so the age of the data is visible.

issues.claim: Finding 7 (cold email) rated 'Medium (not High) only because of the size of the dataset'
issues.problem: Not a factual error, but the strength rating sits above the brief's own rule set: this is vendor-published, unaudited, self-interested data (the TNW article is written by Belkins' CMO about Belkins' own campaigns), and the brief elsewhere calls comparable vendor data Low. The brief does disclose the vendor status in the same cell and in the caveats, and the underlying Belkins methodology page (7,530,489 emails, 34,393 replies, replies / total emails sent to net-new contacts, 0.50% H1, 0.40% H2, 0.35% December) matches exactly.
issues.fix: Either downgrade to Low with the volume argument stated as 'large but unaudited vendor dataset', or add one sentence explaining why volume alone justifies Medium over the Low given to Thryv.

issues.claim: Finding 8: 'Of 4 pilots, 2 finished and both became paid clients'
issues.problem: Partly inferred. The source lists the BOFU steps as 4 clients onboarded / 2 pilots finished (2 stopped early) / 2 paid clients, and separately says 'every client that we have managed to drive results for ended up signing up for the paid plan.' The page never states outright that the two paid clients are the two that finished.
issues.fix: Reword as '2 of 4 pilots finished and 2 clients converted to paid (the source implies these are the same two, but does not say so explicitly)'. The numbers 4, 2, 2 and the 10+ hour setup cost are all confirmed.

issues.claim: Recommendation 8: 'because Hinge found buyers willing to refer but firms almost never asking'
issues.problem: Overstated in paraphrase. The source says 69% of buyers are very willing to recommend, and that when buyers do not refer, 'almost three quarters of the time' the reason is that nobody asked. 'Almost never' is stronger than 'roughly three quarters of the time'. Finding 4 states this correctly.
issues.fix: Change to 'firms fail to ask roughly three quarters of the time' so the recommendation matches the finding's wording.
